sanskrit: rātrī mātā nabhaḥ pitā- -aryamā te pitāmahaḥ | śilācī nāma vā asi sā devānām asi svasā ||
english: Night is your mother, the Sky your father, Aryamā is your grandfather. Śilācī indeed is your name; you are the sister of the gods.

sanskrit: yas tvā pibati jīvati trāyase puruṣaṃ tvam | dhartrī ca śaśvatām asi śaśvatāṃ ca nyañcanī ||
english: Whoever drinks you lives; you protect the man. You are the upholder of the eternal ones, and the binder of the eternal ones.

sanskrit: yad daṇḍena yad iṣvā yad arur harasā kṛtam | tasya tvam asi bheṣajī niṣkṛtir nāma vā asi ||
english: Whatever has been done by a staff, or by an arrow, or by a wound with burning heat — for that you are the healer; Niṣkṛti indeed is your name.

sanskrit: bhadrā plakṣe ni tiṣṭhasy aśvatthe khadire dhave | bhadrā nyagrodhe parṇe sā na ehy arundhati ||
english: Auspiciously you abide on the plakṣa, on the aśvattha, on the khadira, on the dhava; auspiciously on the nyagrodha tree. Come to us, O Arundhatī!

sanskrit: vṛkṣaṃvṛkṣam ā rohasi vṛṣaṇyantīva kanyalā | jayantī pratyātiṣṭhantī saṃjayā nāma vā asi ||
english: Tree by tree you climb, like a maiden in her ardour. Victorious, standing firm against all, Saṃjayā indeed is your name.

sanskrit: hiraṇyavarṇe yuvate śuṣme lomaśavakṣaṇe | apām asi svasā lākṣe vāto hātmā babhūva te ||
english: O golden-hued young one, vigorous, with a hairy flank — O Lākṣā, you are the sister of the waters; the wind has become your very breath.

sanskrit: hiraṇyabāho subhage sūryavarṇe vapuṣṭame | rutaṃ gacchati niṣkṛtiḥ semaṃ niṣkṛdhi pūruṣam ||
english: O golden-armed, blessed one, of the sun's colour, most beautiful in form — the expiation goes where it must go; expiate this man here.

sanskrit: ghṛtācī nāma kānīno 'jababhru pitā tava | aśvo yamasya yaḥ śyāvas tasya hāsnāsy ukṣitā ||
english: Ghṛtācī by name is the illegitimate child; Ajababhru is your father. You are the blood of that dark horse of Yama — so are you infused.

sanskrit: aśvasyāsnaḥ saṃpatitā sā parṇam abhi ṣiṣyadaḥ | sarā patatriṇy asi sā na ehy arundhati ||
english: Fallen together from the blood of the horse, she has clung to the leaf. You are a flowing, winged one; come to us, O Arundhatī!

sanskrit: ghṛtācike vātarathe vidyutparṇe arundhati | āturaṃ gamiṣṭhāsi tvam aṅga niṣkarīyasī ||
english: O Ghṛtācikā, who rides the wind-chariot, whose wings are lightning, O Arundhatī — you go most readily to the afflicted; verily you shall carry him away from pain.

sanskrit: yat te jagdhaṃ piśācais tat ta ā pyāyatāṃ punaḥ | lākṣā tvā viśvabheṣajī devebhis trāyatāṃ saha ||
english: Whatever of you has been consumed by the Piśācas, let that swell up again for you. May Lākṣā, the all-healer, protect you together with the gods.

sanskrit: yathā dyauś ca pṛthivī ca na bibhīto na riṣyataḥ | evā me prāṇa mā bibher evā me 'pāna mā riṣaḥ ||
english: As Heaven and Earth do not fear and do not perish, even so, O my in-breath, do not fear; O my out-breath, do not fail.

sanskrit: yathā vāyuś cāntarikṣaṃ ca (…) ||
english: As Wind and the Atmosphere do not fear and do not perish, even so, O my in-breath, do not fear; O my out-breath, do not fail.

sanskrit: yathā sūryaś ca candramāś ca (…) ||
english: As the Sun and the Moon do not fear and do not perish, even so, O my in-breath, do not fear; O my out-breath, do not fail.

sanskrit: yathāhaś ca rātrī ca (…) ||
english: As Day and Night do not fear and do not perish, even so, O my in-breath, do not fear; O my out-breath, do not fail.

sanskrit: yathā dhenuś cānaḍvāṃś ca (…) ||
english: As the cow and the bull do not fear and do not perish, even so, O my in-breath, do not fear; O my out-breath, do not fail.

sanskrit: yathā mitraś ca varuṇaś ca (…) ||
english: As Mitra and Varuṇa do not fear and do not perish, even so, O my in-breath, do not fear; O my out-breath, do not fail.

sanskrit: yathā brahma ca kṣatraṃ ca (…) ||
english: As the brahman and the kṣatra do not fear and do not perish, even so, O my in-breath, do not fear; O my out-breath, do not fail.

sanskrit: yathendraś cendriyaṃ ca (…) ||
english: As Indra and his sovereign power do not fear and do not perish, even so, O my in-breath, do not fear; O my out-breath, do not fail.

sanskrit: yathā vīraś ca vīryaṃ ca (…) ||
english: As the hero and heroic might do not fear and do not perish, even so, O my in-breath, do not fear; O my out-breath, do not fail.

sanskrit: yathā prāṇaś cāpānaś ca (…) ||
english: As the in-breath and the out-breath do not fear and do not perish, even so, O my in-breath, do not fear; O my out-breath, do not fail.

sanskrit: yathā mṛtyuś cāmṛtaṃ ca (…) ||
english: As Death and Immortality do not fear and do not perish, even so, O my in-breath, do not fear; O my out-breath, do not fail.

sanskrit: yathā satyaṃ cānṛtaṃ ca (…) ||
english: As Truth and Untruth do not fear and do not perish, even so, O my in-breath, do not fear; O my out-breath, do not fail.

sanskrit: yathā bhūtaṃ ca bhavyaṃ ca na bibhīto na riṣyataḥ | evā me prāṇa mā bibher evā me 'pāna mā riṣaḥ ||
english: As what has been and what shall be do not fear and do not perish, even so, O my in-breath, do not fear; O my out-breath, do not fail.

sanskrit: madhuman me nikramaṇaṃ madhuman me parāyaṇam | vācā madhumad udyāsam akṣyau me madhusaṃdṛśī ||
english: Honey-sweet is my going forth, honey-sweet is my going onward; may I speak with a honey-sweet voice; may my two eyes be honeyed in appearance.

sanskrit: mām anu prasārayan mama patto nipedivān | atho me punar āyato akṣyau kāmena śuṣyatām ||
english: He who stretches out toward me, who has fallen at my feet — and he who has come back again to me — may his two eyes wither with longing.

sanskrit: vaśā madhugha te mātā- -ukṣā bhrātarṣabhaḥ pitā | dhenvā adhi prajāto 'si rājā san madhumattamaḥ ||
english: A barren cow is your mother, O Madhu-substance; a potent bull-ox is your father. You are born from a milch-cow; being a king, you are most laden with sweetness.

sanskrit: vṛṣāṇaṃ vṛṣṇyāvantaṃ somapṛṣṭhaṃ divi śritam | indrāṇy agra ābharan madhughaṃ bhagāya kam ||
english: The bull-like one possessed of virile power, soma-backed, dwelling in the sky — Indrāṇī brought forward the honey-substance first of all, for the sake of good fortune.

sanskrit: pitubhojano madhughaḥ śauṣkāsyo hṛdayāya kam | sa mā madhunānaktu yathāhaṃ kāmaye tathā ||
english: The honey-substance that feeds on food, the one with a dry mouth — for the heart, indeed. May it anoint me with sweetness, so that I may obtain what I desire.

sanskrit: sindhuprajāno madhugho aśva iva nīyate janām̐ anu | sa mā (…) ||
english: The honey-substance, born of the river, is led among people like a horse. May it anoint me with sweetness, so that I may obtain what I desire.

sanskrit: madhumatī sinīvālī madhunā mā sam ukṣatu | sā mā madhunānaktu yathāhaṃ kāmaye tathā ||
english: May sweet Sinīvālī sprinkle me together with sweetness. May she anoint me with sweetness, so that I may obtain what I desire.

sanskrit: yathā madhu madhukṛto nyañjanti madhāv adhi | evā ny anajmi te mano adhy asyāṃ māmakī tanū ||
english: Just as the bees anoint honey upon honey, so do I anoint your mind upon this body of mine.

sanskrit: yat te manaḥ parāgataṃ yad baddham iha veha vā | tat ta ā vartayāmasi mayi badhnāmi te manaḥ ||
english: Whatever of your mind has gone away, whatever is bound here or elsewhere — that I turn back to you; within me I bind your mind.
